Question Choices: How many complex roots does a cubic polynomial have, counting multiplicity?
Hints: The degree is 3.|Apply the fundamental theorem of algebra.
Solution: The fundamental theorem of algebra says a nonconstant degree-n polynomial with complex coefficients has exactly n complex roots counting multiplicity. Real roots are included among complex roots. Repeated roots need not be distinct; the leading coefficient multiplies the complete linear factorization. A cubic has three complex roots counting multiplicity.

Question Choices: Select. Can a real quadratic have exactly one non-real root? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Non-real roots of real polynomials come in conjugate pairs.|One alone is impossible.
Solution: For real coefficients, every nonreal root occurs with its complex conjugate and the same multiplicity. Question Choices: The polynomial (x - 2)^3 has how many distinct roots?
Hints: The only root is 2.|Its multiplicity is 3.
Solution: The multiplicity of root a is the highest exponent m such that (x-a)^m divides the polynomial. Count the root once for distinct-root counts, but m times when counting multiplicity. There is one distinct root, x = 2.
